places.tip: Engage in thrilling water sports like paddleboarding, kayaking, and jet skiing directly on Gwangalli Beach. Booking in advance is recommended, especially during peak season.

places.name: 더박스
places.tip: This multi-purpose complex features art exhibitions, unique shops, and cafes, offering a cultural respite from the beach. It's an excellent spot to discover local art and find distinctive gifts.

places.name: 남천동 벚꽃거리
places.tip: Visit in early spring (late March to early April) to experience a breathtaking tunnel of cherry blossoms, perfect for a leisurely stroll and photography. It's a short walk from Gwangalli Beach.

places.name: 금련산
places.tip: Hike up Geumnyeonsan for panoramic views of Gwangalli Beach, Gwangan Bridge, and the Busan cityscape. Wear comfortable shoes and allow 2-3 hours for a rewarding round trip.

marketingCopy: Experience the vibrant energy of Gwangalli, where the iconic Gwangan Bridge illuminates the night sky and sandy beaches invite relaxation. Indulge in fresh seafood, explore trendy cafes, and discover unique cultural spots, making it a perfect blend of modern charm and traditional allure.

places.name: BIFF 광장
places.tip: Famous for street food like Ssiat Hotteok (sweet pancake with seeds). Try to visit in the late afternoon or evening for the liveliest atmosphere and best street food options.

places.name: 자갈치시장
places.tip: Experience the vibrant market on the first floor, then choose fresh seafood to be cooked upstairs at one of the many restaurants. Prices are negotiable, so don't be afraid to haggle a bit.

places.name: 국제시장
places.tip: Explore the labyrinthine alleys for a wide variety of goods, from traditional Korean items to imported products. It's a great place to find unique souvenirs and experience a traditional Korean market.

places.name: 용두산공원 & 부산타워
places.tip: Take the escalator up from Nampo-dong for easy access. Entry to Busan Tower costs around 12,000 KRW, offering panoramic views of Busan, especially stunning at sunset.

places.name: 남포동 지하상가
places.tip: A perfect spot for budget-friendly fashion, cosmetics, and accessories, especially useful on rainy or very hot days. Most shops accept credit cards, but cash might offer better deals.

places.name: 롯데백화점 광복점
places.tip: Beyond shopping, don't miss the impressive musical fountain show in the basement (check schedule) and the rooftop park for great views of the harbor and Busan Tower.

places.name: 부평깡통시장 (야시장)
places.tip: Visit in the evening (from around 7 PM) to experience the lively night market with diverse international and Korean street foods. Be prepared for crowds and long queues for popular stalls.

places.name: 부산근대역사관
places.tip: This museum offers free entry and provides fascinating insights into Busan's modern history, particularly during the Japanese colonial period and the Korean War. English explanations are available.

places.name: 남포동 먹자골목
places.tip: Specifically dedicated to the vibrant street food scene. Try tteokbokki, odeng, gyeranppang (egg bread), and various fried snacks. It's a great way to sample many local delicacies quickly.

places.name: 카페 리프
places.tip: A popular cafe known for its cozy atmosphere and delicious desserts, perfect for a relaxing break from shopping and sightseeing. Look for it in one of Nampo-dong's charming side streets.

marketingCopy: Nampo-dong, the bustling heart of Busan's Jung-gu district, offers an exhilarating blend of traditional markets, modern shopping, and delectable street food. Immerse yourself in the vibrant energy, explore historical sites, and savor unique culinary delights.

places.name: 어린왕자와 사막여우 포토존
places.nameEn: The Little Prince and the Fox Photo Zone
places.tip: This iconic spot offers the most famous panoramic views of the village. Be prepared for a queue, especially on weekends and holidays, but the photo opportunity is worth the wait.

places.name: 감천문화마을 안내센터
places.tip: Start your visit here to grab a map (available for a small fee, typically 2,000 KRW) and participate in the stamp tour, which guides you through key attractions and offers a small prize upon completion.

places.name: 하늘마루 전망대
places.tip: Located at the highest point, this observatory offers stunning 360-degree views of the entire village and the distant sea. It's a great spot for panoramic photos without the crowds of the Little Prince area.

places.name: 아방가르드 카페
places.tip: Enjoy a coffee or local snack while taking in breathtaking views of the colorful houses from its terrace. It's a perfect spot to rest your legs after exploring the village's hilly paths.

places.name: 감내어울터
places.tip: This former public bathhouse now houses art galleries, souvenir shops, and sometimes workshops. Look for unique handmade crafts and local artworks here.

places.name: 감천벽화마을 골목길
places.tip: Dedicate time to wander aimlessly through the narrow, winding alleys to discover hidden murals, quirky sculptures, and charming small shops. Wear comfortable shoes as the village is very hilly.

places.name: 감천문화마을 붕어빵
places.tip: Try the unique fish-shaped bread (Bungeoppang) filled with various sweet or savory fillings, often sold by street vendors. It's a classic Korean snack perfect for a quick energy boost.

places.name: 어둠의 집
places.tip: Enter this intriguing art installation to experience a sensory journey in complete darkness. It offers a different perspective and a unique artistic experience for a small entry fee (usually 2,000 KRW).

places.name: 감천 기념품샵
places.tip: Browse the various souvenir shops scattered throughout the village for unique handmade items, postcards, and local crafts that capture the essence of Gamcheon.

places.name: 감천문화마을 추억사진관
places.tip: Rent a traditional Korean hanbok or a retro school uniform to enhance your photo experience. Many shops offer rental services for a few hours, perfect for creating memorable pictures against the colorful backdrop.

marketingCopy: Step into a vibrant fairytale at Gamcheon Culture Village, a former hillside slum transformed into a whimsical labyrinth of colorful houses, quirky cafes, and captivating street art, offering endless photo opportunities and unique cultural experiences.

places.name: 송정해수욕장
places.tip: Visit during summer for swimming and sunbathing, or in spring/autumn for surfing. Public showers and changing rooms are available, and many surf shops offer board rentals and lessons starting from around KRW 50,000.

places.name: 죽도공원
places.tip: Enjoy a scenic walk through this small pine forest park located on a peninsula at the northern end of Songjeong Beach. Climb to the pavilion for panoramic views of the ocean and beach, especially beautiful at sunrise.

places.name: 구 송정역
places.tip: Explore this beautifully preserved old train station, now a cultural space and photo zone. It's a charming spot to reflect on the area's history and take unique pictures, especially popular with couples.

places.name: 송정 서핑 체험
places.tip: Songjeong is Busan's premier surfing spot, perfect for beginners due to its gentle waves. Many schools along the beach offer lessons and equipment rentals; expect to pay around KRW 50,000-70,000 for a beginner's package including instruction and board.

places.name: 포트1902
places.tip: This trendy cafe and lounge offers stunning ocean views and a luxurious atmosphere, perfect for relaxing after a day at the beach. They also have a pool area (check for entry fees/minimum spend) and sometimes host DJ events in the evening.

places.name: 카페윤
places.tip: Another popular cafe known for its beautiful aesthetics and direct beach views. It's a great spot to enjoy a coffee or dessert while watching the surfers, especially during sunset.

places.name: 송정집
places.tip: Try the local specialty 'Guksu' (noodles) at this popular restaurant, known for its hearty and delicious dishes. Expect a short wait during peak meal times, but the fresh ingredients and unique flavors are worth it.

places.name: 명랑핫도그 송정점
places.tip: Grab a quick and delicious Korean-style corn dog, a popular street food snack, perfect for a budget-friendly bite near the beach. Customize it with various sauces and toppings for a unique flavor experience.

places.name: 송정 서핑 장비 렌탈
places.tip: For spontaneous surfing, numerous shops along the beach offer wetsuit and board rentals by the hour or day. Prices usually range from KRW 20,000-40,000 for a few hours, perfect for experienced surfers or those who've taken lessons.

places.name: 송정어촌계공동판매장
places.tip: Experience a local taste by visiting this small market where local fishermen sell their fresh catches daily. It's a great place to buy seafood to cook yourself or find a nearby restaurant that can prepare it for you.

marketingCopy: Escape the city bustle at Songjeong Beach, a laid-back coastal haven renowned for its gentle waves perfect for surfing. Discover charming cafes, historic sites, and fresh seafood in this picturesque Haeundae gem.

places.name: 동문시장
places.tip: Experience the vibrant atmosphere and try various street foods like Hallabong juice and tteokbokki. Best visited in the evening for dinner and snacks.

places.name: 흑돼지거리
places.tip: Indulge in Jeju's famous Black Pork BBQ. Expect slightly higher prices, but the quality is excellent. Many restaurants offer combo sets perfect for sharing.

places.name: 국수거리
places.tip: Try Gogi Guksu (pork noodle soup), a Jeju specialty. Most restaurants open for lunch and dinner, offering a hearty and affordable meal.

places.name: 칠성로 상점가
places.tip: Explore fashion boutiques, cosmetics stores, and local shops. It's a pedestrian-friendly street, often featuring street performances on weekends.

places.name: 중앙지하상가
places.tip: A great place to shop for clothes, accessories, and souvenirs, especially on a rainy day. It connects directly to Chilseong-ro Shopping Street.

places.name: 제주국립박물관
places.tip: Learn about Jeju's unique history and culture through artifacts and exhibits. Admission is free. Check their website for temporary exhibitions and opening hours.

places.name: 삼성혈
places.tip: Visit this sacred site where Jeju's three founding ancestors are said to have emerged. The entrance fee is around 4,000 KRW for adults. It's a peaceful historical park.

places.name: 제주목관아
places.tip: Explore the restored former administrative center of Jeju. It offers insights into traditional Korean architecture and governance. Entrance fee is around 1,500 KRW.

places.name: 탑동광장
places.tip: Enjoy a leisurely stroll along the waterfront, watch the sunset, or participate in various recreational activities. Many cafes and restaurants are nearby for refreshments.

places.name: 카페 드 라 피스
places.tip: Relax and enjoy excellent coffee and desserts in a stylish setting after exploring the city center. Many cafes in the area offer unique Jeju-inspired drinks and treats.

marketingCopy: Discover the vibrant heart of Jeju Island in Jeju City Center, where bustling markets, historic sites, and modern shopping districts blend seamlessly with delicious local cuisine.

places.name: 정방폭포
places.tip: This is one of the only waterfalls in Asia that falls directly into the ocean. There's a small entrance fee (around 2,000 KRW for adults); wear comfortable shoes as the path down to the falls can be rocky. Best visited in the morning to avoid crowds.

places.name: 천지연폭포
places.tip: Enjoy a leisurely stroll through the beautiful park leading to the waterfall, which is illuminated at night for a magical experience. There's an entrance fee (around 2,000 KRW for adults); it's easily accessible by public bus or taxi from Seogwipo city center.

places.name: 이중섭거리
places.tip: Explore this charming street dedicated to the famous artist Lee Jung-seop, featuring galleries, cafes, and unique souvenir shops. Visit on a weekend for street performances and a lively atmosphere; many small cafes offer great local coffee and treats.

places.name: 서귀포매일올레시장
places.tip: Immerse yourself in local culture and try delicious street food like Hallabong juice, black pork skewers, and various fresh seafood. It's a great place to buy local specialties and souvenirs; arrive hungry and bring cash for some vendors.

places.name: 외돌개
places.tip: Enjoy breathtaking coastal views and a leisurely walk along the Olle Trail segment surrounding this iconic rock formation. There's no entrance fee; parking is available, and it's particularly scenic during sunset.

places.name: 새연교 & 새섬
places.tip: Walk across Korea's longest pedestrian bridge, designed in the shape of a Teu (traditional Jeju boat), to explore the small, tranquil Saeseom Island. The bridge is beautifully lit at night, offering fantastic photo opportunities; combine this with a visit to Cheonjiyeon Waterfall nearby.

places.name: 카페 바다다
places.tip: Indulge in coffee or cocktails with stunning panoramic ocean views from this trendy cafe, known for its stylish interior and outdoor seating. It can get very busy, especially on weekends, so consider visiting during off-peak hours for a more relaxed experience.

places.name: 흑돼지거리
places.tip: Savor the unique taste of Jeju's famous black pork at one of the many specialized restaurants along this street. Expect higher prices for this local delicacy, but the quality and flavor are worth it; many restaurants provide English menus.

places.name: 약천사
places.tip: Visit this grand Buddhist temple, notable for its impressive size and beautiful architecture, including a towering main hall. There's no entrance fee; remember to be respectful of the sacred space and dress modestly when entering temple buildings.

places.name: 서귀포잠수함
places.tip: Experience the underwater world of Seogwipo without getting wet on this unique submarine tour, offering views of colorful fish and coral reefs. Booking in advance is highly recommended, especially during peak season; check their website for operating hours and fees (around 60,000 KRW for adults).

marketingCopy: Discover Seogwipo, the vibrant southern heart of Jeju, where stunning waterfalls meet the ocean and cultural streets buzz with art. This guide will lead you through breathtaking natural wonders, authentic local markets, and unique culinary delights.

places.name: 한담 해안산책로
places.tip: Enjoy a leisurely stroll along this beautiful coastal path connecting Gwakji Beach to Aewol Port, offering breathtaking ocean views and access to many popular cafes. It's free and best visited during sunset for stunning photo opportunities.

places.name: 봄날카페
places.tip: A very popular cafe known for its vibrant decor and direct ocean views. Be prepared for crowds, especially on weekends; aim for a weekday morning visit for a more relaxed experience.

places.name: 몽상드애월
places.tip: Famous for its modern architecture and scenic oceanfront location, this cafe offers great photo opportunities. Parking can be challenging, so consider taking a taxi or public bus (routes 202, 291, 292) to Aewol-ri.

places.name: 곽지과물해변
places.tip: A beautiful white sand beach with unique naturally filtered spring water pools, perfect for swimming and relaxation. Free to enter, it's ideal for a refreshing dip during summer afternoons.

places.name: 애월 한치초밥
places.tip: Try the local specialty, Hanchi Chobap (squid sushi), known for its fresh taste and unique texture. This restaurant is popular, so consider visiting outside peak lunch or dinner hours to avoid long waits.

places.name: 애월더선셋
places.tip: A fantastic spot to enjoy a meal or coffee with panoramic ocean views, especially stunning during sunset. Reservations are recommended for dinner to secure a good table.

places.name: 돈사돈 애월점
places.tip: Savor authentic Jeju Black Pork BBQ at this renowned restaurant. Expect a lively atmosphere and potential wait times, especially in the evenings; a hearty meal usually costs around 25,000-35,000 KRW per person.

places.name: 애월읍 5일장
places.tip: Experience a traditional Korean market where locals sell fresh produce, seafood, and various goods. The market operates on days ending in 2 and 7 (e.g., 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, 27th of the month); check the specific dates before your visit.

places.name: 제주마공원
places.tip: Enjoy a unique horseback riding experience amidst Jeju's scenic landscapes, suitable for all skill levels. Prices vary depending on the course length, typically starting from 15,000 KRW for a short ride.

places.name: 애월항
places.tip: Wander around this charming fishing port to observe local life, colorful boats, and enjoy the calm sea breeze. It's a great spot for a peaceful walk and offers picturesque views, especially during sunrise or sunset.

marketingCopy: Discover Aewol, Jeju-si's picturesque coastal haven, where charming cafes meet stunning ocean views and a relaxed atmosphere. Indulge in local delicacies, stroll along scenic paths, and immerse yourself in Jeju's unique island life.

places.name: 성산일출봉
places.tip: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for breathtaking sunrises. Arrive early for the best views; admission fee is 5,000 KRW for adults. Wear comfortable shoes for the climb.

places.name: 성산해녀의집
places.tip: Enjoy extremely fresh seafood caught by Jeju's famous Haenyeo divers. Try the grilled abalone or sea urchin bibimbap for an authentic taste of Jeju.

places.name: 광치기해변
places.tip: Offers a unique view of Seongsan Ilchulbong, especially stunning at low tide when volcanic rock formations are exposed. It's a popular spot for photography and horse riding.

places.name: 아쿠아플라넷 제주
places.tip: One of Asia's largest aquariums, featuring diverse marine life and exciting performances. Great for families; check the official website for show times and ticket prices (approx. 40,000 KRW for adults).

places.name: 우도 도항선 터미널
places.tip: The gateway to Udo Island. Catch a ferry for a charming day trip; you can rent bicycles or scooters on Udo to explore its scenic routes and beautiful beaches.

places.name: 해맞이 카페
places.tip: Relax with a coffee or local Jeju beverage while enjoying panoramic views of Seongsan Ilchulbong and the vast ocean. Perfect for a morning or afternoon break.

places.name: 섭지코지
places.tip: A picturesque cape known for its dramatic coastal cliffs, a historic lighthouse, and as a popular filming location. Enjoy a leisurely walk along the scenic trails.

places.name: 성산오일장
places.tip: Experience a vibrant traditional Korean market (held on days ending in 0 and 5). Find fresh local produce, street food, and unique Jeju souvenirs.

places.name: 곰막식당
places.tip: A beloved local eatery famous for its fresh mackerel sashimi noodles (고등어회국수) and comforting sea urchin seaweed soup. It can get busy, so be prepared for a short wait.

places.name: 글라스하우스 & 유민미술관
places.nameEn: Glass House & Yumin Art Nouveau Collection
places.tip: Marvel at Tadao Ando's architectural masterpiece and explore the exquisite collection of Art Nouveau glass art. Offers stunning views of the coastline; check for specific museum opening hours and fees.

marketingCopy: Experience the majestic beauty of Seongsan Ilchulbong, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and explore the captivating coastal wonders, unique local culture, and delicious seafood of eastern Jeju Island.

places.name: 협재해변
places.tip: Enjoy the free entry to this stunning beach with emerald waters and white sand. Best visited during low tide to walk closer to Biyangdo Island, or for a beautiful sunset view. Public buses stop conveniently at the beach.

places.name: 한림공원
places.tip: Entry fee is approximately 13,000 KRW for adults. Visit in the morning to explore its diverse botanical gardens, lava caves, and folk village before it gets too crowded, offering a tranquil experience.

places.name: 금능해변
places.tip: This beautiful beach, with free entry, is just a short walk from Hyeopjae and often less crowded. It's perfect for a quieter swim or enjoying the clear, shallow turquoise waters ideal for families.

places.name: 쉼표, 협재
places.tip: Relax with a coffee or dessert while enjoying panoramic views of Hyeopjae Beach and Biyangdo Island. It's an ideal spot to unwind after swimming or exploring the coastal area.

places.name: 협재해녀의집
places.tip: Savor incredibly fresh seafood caught by Jeju's iconic Haenyeo (women divers). This popular restaurant can get busy, so consider visiting during off-peak hours for a shorter wait.

places.name: 오설록 티 뮤지엄
places.tip: Entry to the museum and tea fields is free, though tastings and cafe items are extra. It's best visited on a clear day to fully appreciate the vast green tea plantations, located about a 20-30 minute drive from Hyeopjae.

places.name: 제주유리의성
places.tip: The entry fee is around 12,000 KRW for adults. This unique art park features stunning glass sculptures and installations, providing fantastic photo opportunities, especially when illuminated at night. It's a 15-minute drive from Hyeopjae.

places.name: 한림매일시장
places.tip: Explore this lively traditional market for local produce, fresh seafood, and authentic street food. It's a great place to immerse yourself in local culture and find unique Jeju souvenirs.

places.name: 제주승마공원
places.tip: Experience horse riding with picturesque views of Jeju's landscapes. Prices vary by course duration, typically ranging from 20,000-50,000 KRW. Booking in advance is advisable during peak tourist seasons.

places.name: 제주바당캔들
places.tip: Discover unique, handcrafted candles and diffusers inspired by Jeju's beautiful ocean. These make perfect, memorable gifts and souvenirs to take a piece of Jeju home with you.

marketingCopy: Discover the breathtaking beauty of Hyeopjae Beach, a jewel on Jeju Island renowned for its emerald waters, white sands, and stunning views of Biyangdo Island. Perfect for a relaxing escape, water activities, and exploring charming local cafes and cultural sites.

places.name: 대릉원
places.tip: Entry fee is typically 3,000 KRW for adults. Visit in the morning for fewer crowds and better photo opportunities, as it's easily accessible by foot from other major sites.

places.name: 첨성대
places.tip: There is no separate entry fee as it's an open site. Best visited at sunset or night when it's beautifully lit, creating a magical atmosphere for photos.

places.name: 동궁과 월지
places.tip: Entry fee is around 3,000 KRW for adults. This site is famous for its stunning night views, so plan your visit for after dusk to witness its illuminated beauty.

places.name: 황리단길
places.tip: This trendy street offers unique cafes, restaurants, and shops. It's perfect for an afternoon stroll and trying local snacks, located right next to the major historic sites.

places.name: 계림
places.tip: Free to enter, this ancient forest is steeped in Silla mythology. Enjoy a peaceful walk and imagine the legends within its tranquil surroundings, especially during spring or autumn.

places.name: 국립경주박물관
places.tip: Admission is free, offering an extensive collection of Silla artifacts. Allow at least 2 hours to fully appreciate the exhibits and gain deeper insight into Gyeongju's history.

places.name: 별채반 교동쌈밥
places.tip: Experience traditional Ssambap, a healthy meal with various vegetables and side dishes. It's a popular spot, so consider visiting outside peak lunch/dinner hours to avoid long waits.

places.name: 노워즈
places.tip: Enjoy a modern cafe experience in a traditional setting on Hwanglidan-gil. Great for a coffee break and people-watching after exploring the historic sites.

places.name: 경주 교촌마을
places.tip: Free entry, this village offers a glimpse into traditional Korean life with hanok houses and craft experiences. Don't miss trying the Gyeongju Gyori Gimbap, a local specialty.

places.name: 경주 기념품샵
places.tip: Look for unique Silla-themed souvenirs, such as Cheonmachong-inspired items or local crafts. Many shops are found along Hwanglidan-gil or near the main attractions.

marketingCopy: Step back in time to the ancient Silla kingdom as you explore Gyeongju Historic Area, a UNESCO World Heritage site filled with royal tombs, ancient observatories, and stunning palaces. Discover a blend of rich history and modern charm, perfect for an unforgettable cultural journey.

places.name: 불국사
places.tip: Bulguksa is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Entry is typically 6,000 KRW for adults. Visit early morning or late afternoon to avoid crowds and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

places.name: 석굴암
places.tip: Seokguram Grotto is another UNESCO site, often visited with Bulguksa. You can take a local bus (Bus No. 12) from Bulguksa to Seokguram, which takes about 15-20 minutes. The entry fee is 6,000 KRW.

places.name: 불국사 청운교 백운교
places.nameEn: Bulguksa Cheongun-gyo & Baekun-gyo (Blue Cloud & White Cloud Bridges)
places.tip: These iconic stone bridges at the main entrance of Bulguksa are national treasures. While you cannot walk on them, they offer a magnificent photo opportunity and represent the journey to the Buddhist Pure Land.

places.name: 불국사 기념품점
places.tip: Located within the temple complex, this shop offers a range of Buddhist-themed souvenirs, traditional crafts, and books. It's a great place to find unique gifts and mementos of your visit.

places.name: 토함산식당
places.tip: Enjoy a traditional Korean set meal (Hanjeongsik) with various side dishes. This restaurant is conveniently located near the temple entrance, offering authentic local flavors after your exploration.

places.name: 스타벅스 경주불국사점
places.tip: Grab a familiar coffee or snack at Starbucks, conveniently located just outside the main Bulguksa entrance. It's a comfortable spot to recharge before or after exploring the temple grounds.

places.name: 불국사 관광안내소
places.tip: Before or after your visit, stop here for maps, brochures, and assistance with local transportation or attractions. The staff can provide valuable insights for foreign visitors.

places.name: 불국사 문화재 판매점
places.tip: Find high-quality replicas of cultural artifacts, traditional pottery, and local Gyeongju specialties. This shop offers more curated items compared to general souvenir stalls.

places.name: 불국사 산책로
places.tip: Beyond the main temple structures, explore the peaceful walking trails surrounding Bulguksa. These paths offer beautiful views of the temple and the natural landscape, especially during spring and autumn.

places.name: 불국사 템플스테이 안내
places.tip: For a deeper cultural immersion, inquire about the temple stay program. While not always available for walk-ins, you can get information on how to book an overnight stay to experience monastic life and meditation.

marketingCopy: Step into a realm of ancient beauty at Bulguksa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site showcasing exquisite Silla dynasty architecture and profound Buddhist heritage. Explore its serene grounds and iconic structures for a truly spiritual and historical journey in Gyeongju.

places.name: 양동마을 전체 탐방
places.tip: Purchase your admission ticket (approx. 4,000 KRW for adults) at the entrance. The best times to visit are early morning or late afternoon to avoid crowds and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

places.name: 서백당
places.tip: As a prominent clan head house and private residence, please observe its exterior and courtyard respectfully from designated viewing areas. It embodies the traditional living style of Joseon nobility.

places.name: 무첨당
places.tip: This historic house showcases exquisite Joseon Dynasty architecture. Pay attention to the intricate details and the traditional layout, reflecting the social status and values of its former residents.

places.name: 향단
places.tip: One of the largest and most significant houses, Hyangdan offers a glimpse into the grand lifestyle of Joseon scholars. Its unique 'ㄷ'-shaped layout is a notable architectural feature.

places.name: 관가정
places.tip: Situated on a hillside, Gwangajeong provides stunning panoramic views of the village and surrounding natural beauty. It's an ideal spot for photography, especially during autumn.

places.name: 양동마을 민속박물관
places.tip: Start your visit here to understand the village's history, culture, and the significance of the artifacts displayed in the traditional houses. English explanations are generally available.

places.name: 양동 전통문화체험관
places.tip: Participate in hands-on programs like traditional craft making or tea ceremonies to immerse yourself in Korean culture. Inquire about available programs and booking in advance is recommended.

places.name: 양동마을 식당
places.tip: Enjoy authentic Korean cuisine, such as Bibimbap or local Gyeongju specialties, at one of the village's traditional eateries. Look for signs indicating '식당' (sikdang).

places.name: 카페 양동
places.tip: Take a relaxing break at this charming cafe to savor traditional Korean teas or coffee amidst the historical surroundings. It's a perfect spot to rest and enjoy the peaceful ambiance.

places.name: 양동마을 기념품점
places.tip: Browse for unique souvenirs like traditional pottery, local Gyeongju crafts, or handmade items to remember your visit. Shops are often located near the main entrance or museum.

marketingCopy: Step back in time at Yangdong Folk Village, a UNESCO World Heritage site where traditional Joseon Dynasty homes are nestled in a picturesque valley. Experience the living history and serene beauty of Korea's past.

places.name: 경기전
places.tip: Entry fee is typically around 3,000 KRW. Visit in the morning for fewer crowds and better photo opportunities, especially if you're wearing a hanbok.

places.name: 전동성당
places.tip: Free to enter the grounds, but check specific visiting hours for the interior. Its stunning Romanesque architecture makes it a popular photo spot, especially beautiful at sunset.

places.name: 전주향교
places.tip: Admission is free. This historical Confucian school is famous for its ancient ginkgo trees, which are particularly magnificent in autumn. It's a peaceful escape from the bustling village center.

places.name: 오목대 이목대
places.tip: Free to access. Climb to the top of Omokdae for breathtaking panoramic views of the entire Hanok Village, offering fantastic photo opportunities. Best visited during clear daylight hours.

places.name: 한국집
places.tip: Expect a wait during peak lunch and dinner times, as this is one of Jeonju's oldest and most renowned bibimbap restaurants. Be sure to try their traditional Jeonju Bibimbap for an authentic experience.

places.name: 교동떡갈비
places.tip: Tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties) is a must-try Jeonju specialty. This restaurant serves a delicious version, often accompanied by a generous array of banchan (side dishes). Consider visiting slightly off-peak to avoid queues.

places.name: PNB 풍년제과
places.tip: Famous for its original Jeonju Choco Pies, which make an excellent souvenir. Be prepared for long lines, especially on weekends, but service is efficient. They also offer other traditional Korean pastries.

places.name: 교동다원
places.tip: Experience a tranquil traditional Korean tea ceremony in a beautiful hanok setting. It's a perfect spot to relax and sample various traditional teas and accompanying snacks. Cash payment might be preferred here.

places.name: 한복남 전주한옥마을점
places.tip: Renting a hanbok is a popular and fun way to immerse yourself in the village's atmosphere and take memorable photos. Rental prices typically start from 15,000 KRW for two hours, with options for hair styling.

places.name: 전주전통술박물관
places.tip: Admission is free. Learn about the history and production of traditional Korean alcoholic beverages like makgeolli and cheongju. Occasional tasting sessions are available for a small fee, providing a unique cultural insight.

marketingCopy: Step back in time at Jeonju Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved hub of traditional Korean culture and architecture. Indulge in authentic Jeonju cuisine, explore historic sites, and immerse yourself in the charm of a bygone era.

places.name: 오목대
places.tip: Best visited at sunset for panoramic views of Jeonju Hanok Village. It's free to enter and easily accessible by foot from the village.

places.name: 경기전
places.tip: Entry fee is around 3,000 KRW. Visit in the morning to avoid crowds and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere of this historic royal shrine and its bamboo forest.

places.name: 전동성당
places.tip: Admire the beautiful Romanesque architecture, one of Korea's most stunning churches. It's free to enter, but check service times to avoid disruption.

places.name: 전주한옥마을
places.tip: Spend several hours wandering the charming alleyways, discovering hidden cafes and artisan shops. Consider renting a Hanbok for a unique photo opportunity.

places.name: 한복대여점 (다양한 상점)
places.tip: Renting a traditional Korean Hanbok adds a fun, immersive element to your visit. Prices vary, but expect to pay around 15,000-30,000 KRW for a 2-3 hour rental.

places.name: PNB 풍년제과 본점
places.nameEn: PNB Poongnyeon Jeonju Choco Pie Main Store
places.tip: Don't leave Jeonju without trying their famous handmade Choco Pie, a local specialty. It makes for a delicious souvenir or snack.

places.name: 가족회관
places.tip: Experience authentic Jeonju Bibimbap, a must-try dish. Expect to pay around 10,000-15,000 KRW per person; try to visit outside peak lunch/dinner hours to avoid long queues.

places.name: 다우랑
places.tip: Sample their popular shrimp dumplings (새우만두), a unique and tasty street food snack in the Hanok Village. They often sell out, so visit earlier in the day.

places.name: 카페 전망
places.tip: Enjoy a coffee or traditional tea with stunning panoramic views of the entire Jeonju Hanok Village. It's an ideal spot for relaxation and photography.

places.name: 전주공예품전시관
places.nameEn: Jeonju Traditional Craft Works Exhibition Hall
places.tip: Discover exquisite traditional Korean crafts, including pottery, paper art, and fans, perfect for unique souvenirs. Many items are handmade by local artisans.

marketingCopy: Nestled atop a hill overlooking the historic Jeonju Hanok Village, Omokdae offers breathtaking views and a glimpse into Korea's rich past. Immerse yourself in traditional culture, savor local delicacies, and create unforgettable memories in this charming city.

places.name: 메타세쿼이아길
places.tip: This iconic tree-lined path is perfect for photos, especially in autumn and winter. Rent a bike or walk slowly to fully enjoy the serene atmosphere.

places.name: 은행나무길
places.tip: Visit in late October to early November to witness the stunning golden foliage. It's less crowded early in the morning for the best photo opportunities.

places.name: 겨울연가 첫 키스 촬영지
places.tip: A must-visit for K-drama fans, this spot commemorates a famous scene from 'Winter Sonata.' Take a memorable photo with the statues.

places.name: 나미화랑 & 공예원
places.tip: Browse unique, handmade souvenirs and local crafts here. It's a great place to find gifts that capture the island's artistic spirit.

places.name: 노래박물관
places.tip: Explore exhibits dedicated to music and sound, often featuring interactive displays. Entry is usually included with island admission, offering a cultural break.

places.name: 그림책놀이터 (Picture Book Library)
places.tip: A charming spot for families with children, offering a quiet place to read and enjoy international picture books. It's a nice refuge on a hot or cold day.

places.name: 동문식당
places.tip: Enjoy traditional Korean dishes, including Chuncheon's specialty, dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken). Prices are reasonable for a tourist spot on the island.

places.name: 연가지가 (Sonata Cafe)
places.tip: Relax with a coffee or tea in this cozy cafe, famous for its 'Winter Sonata' connection. It's a good place to warm up in winter or cool down in summer.

places.name: 자전거 대여소
places.tip: Rent single, tandem, or family bikes to explore the island at your own pace. Rental fees vary, typically starting from 4,000 KRW for 30 minutes.

places.name: 스토리투어버스
places.tip: A convenient way to see the island's highlights if you prefer not to walk or bike the entire distance. Tickets can be purchased at the main information center.

marketingCopy: Escape to Nami Island, a half-moon shaped isle renowned for its stunning natural beauty and as the iconic filming location for the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.' Perfect for a day trip, immerse yourself in picturesque tree-lined paths, cultural exhibits, and charming cafes.

places.name: 공동경비구역 (JSA) 판문점
places.tip: Access is strictly via authorized tours only; book well in advance and bring your passport for security checks. Photography is restricted in certain areas for safety.

places.name: 임진각 평화누리공원
places.tip: Easily accessible and free to enter, this park offers memorials and art installations related to the Korean War and reunification. Allow time to explore the various monuments and enjoy the open space.

places.name: 제3땅굴
places.tip: Entry requires purchasing a ticket as part of a DMZ tour package. Be prepared for a steep descent and ascent; a shuttle train is available for those with mobility issues, but walking is the primary way to experience the tunnel.

places.name: 도라산 전망대
places.tip: Part of most DMZ tours, it offers a rare opportunity to view North Korean territory through binoculars. The best time to visit is on a clear day for optimal visibility across the border.

places.name: 도라산역
places.tip: A symbolic station aspiring to connect the Korean peninsula to Europe, it's a poignant stop on DMZ tours. You can purchase a commemorative ticket, but active train services to North Korea are not available.

places.name: 통일대교
places.tip: This bridge serves as the entry point into the Civilian Control Zone. You can only cross it as part of an official DMZ tour, where soldiers will check your identification.

places.name: 파주 프리미엄 아울렛
places.tip: Located a short drive from the DMZ area, this large outlet mall offers a wide selection of international and local brands. It's a great option for shopping after a historical tour.

places.name: 헤이리 예술마을
places.tip: A unique village dedicated to art and culture, featuring galleries, museums, cafes, and workshops. You can easily spend half a day exploring its diverse attractions; many cafes offer unique local treats.

places.name: 프로방스 마을
places.tip: Inspired by French villages, this colorful area is perfect for a leisurely stroll, dining at charming restaurants, or enjoying a coffee. It's especially beautiful in the evening with its lights.

places.name: 오두산 통일전망대
places.tip: Offering panoramic views of the Han River and North Korean territory, this observatory is an alternative to Dora Observatory and is more accessible for independent visitors without a full DMZ tour.

marketingCopy: Step into a poignant chapter of history at the DMZ Panmunjom, where the echoes of division meet hopes for peace. Experience a unique journey through a divided land, offering deep insights into inter-Korean relations and a glimpse into North Korea.

places.name: 화성
places.tip: Walk the entire 5.7km fortress wall for stunning views; the full course ticket is 1,000 KRW, allowing access to key gates and structures. Best visited in spring or autumn for pleasant weather, with the evening offering beautiful nightscapes.

places.name: 화성행궁
places.tip: This temporary palace for King Jeongjo costs 1,500 KRW for entry. Don't miss the daily Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (check times online) for a vibrant cultural experience.

places.name: 연무대
places.tip: Try traditional Korean archery for 2,000 KRW for 10 arrows. It's a fun, hands-on experience and a great photo opportunity, easily accessible from Changnyongmun Gate.

places.name: 플라잉수원
places.tip: Enjoy panoramic views of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress from above for 18,000 KRW (adults). Consider booking in advance, especially for sunset flights, to guarantee a spot.

places.name: 지동시장
places.tip: Explore this bustling traditional market adjacent to Paldalmun Gate. It's a fantastic spot to try various Korean street foods like tteokbokki and sundae, and find affordable local produce.

places.name: 팔달문
places.tip: As the southern main gate of Hwaseong Fortress, Paldalmun is a magnificent structure and a central landmark. It's particularly beautiful when illuminated at night, offering great photo opportunities.

places.name: 가보정 갈비
places.tip: Savor authentic Suwon galbi (marinated beef ribs), a local specialty, though it can be pricey (around 40,000-60,000 KRW per serving). Reservations are recommended for dinner, especially on weekends.

places.name: 수원화성박물관
places.tip: Learn about the fascinating history and construction techniques of Hwaseong Fortress for an entry fee of 2,000 KRW. It provides excellent context before or after exploring the fortress itself.

places.name: 행궁동 카페거리
places.tip: Wander through this charming street filled with unique cafes and small boutiques, many offering views of the fortress wall. It's perfect for a relaxing break and finding photogenic spots.

places.name: 수원전통문화관
places.tip: Experience various traditional Korean cultural activities, from tea ceremonies to craft workshops (check their schedule and fees online). It's a great way to immerse yourself in local customs near the fortress.

marketingCopy: Step back in time at Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage site showcasing Joseon Dynasty's architectural brilliance. Explore ancient palaces, enjoy traditional experiences, and savor the renowned Suwon Galbi in this vibrant historical city.

places.name: 송도 센트럴파크
places.tip: Enjoy a serene water taxi ride (approx. 4,000-6,000 KRW) for unique city views. Best visited in the morning or late afternoon for pleasant weather and beautiful light.

places.name: G타워
places.tip: Head to the 33rd-floor observation deck for a free panoramic view of Songdo and the Incheon Bridge. Check the IFEZ PR Hall on the lower floors to learn about Songdo's development.

places.name: 트라이볼
places.tip: Admire the unique 'floating' architectural design and check if there are any free art exhibitions or performances inside. It's especially beautiful when lit up at night.

places.name: 엔씨큐브 커낼워크
places.tip: This European-style shopping street is divided into four themed sections (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). Enjoy a leisurely stroll, browse boutique shops, and find many cafes and restaurants along the canal.

places.name: 현대프리미엄아울렛 송도점
places.tip: A large outdoor outlet mall offering a wide range of international and domestic brands with discounts. There's also a food court and various restaurants for a meal or coffee break.

places.name: 미추홀공원
places.tip: Explore a serene park featuring traditional Korean gardens and architecture, offering a peaceful contrast to Songdo's modern cityscape. It's a great spot for a quiet walk or picnic.

places.name: 송도 컨벤시아
places.tip: Appreciate the unique wave-like roof architecture, inspired by traditional Korean curves. While primarily a convention center, it's worth seeing for its design and often hosts public events.

places.name: 카페 코르소
places.tip: Enjoy coffee and desserts with a beautiful view of Songdo Central Park. It's a popular spot for both locals and tourists to relax and people-watch.

places.name: 갈비명가 이상 송도점
places.tip: Savor authentic Korean BBQ in a comfortable setting, specializing in delicious galbi (marinated ribs). Many restaurants in Songdo are foreigner-friendly with English menus available.

places.name: 아트센터 인천
places.tip: Check their schedule for world-class concerts, operas, and ballets, or simply admire the striking architecture of this performing arts complex. Guided tours might be available on specific days.

marketingCopy: Experience the future in Songdo, a master-planned smart city boasting stunning modern architecture, lush green spaces, and a vibrant international community. Enjoy unique waterfront activities, diverse shopping, and innovative cultural attractions.

places.name: 남이섬
places.address: 강원 춘천시 남이섬길 1 (Gapyeong Wharf: 경기도 가평군 가평읍 북한강변로 1024)
places.tip: Famous for K-drama 'Winter Sonata', Nami Island requires a ferry ride from Gapyeong Wharf (round-trip ferry + entrance fee: 16,000 KRW for foreigners). Visit in autumn for stunning foliage or winter for a romantic snowy landscape. Take the Gapyeong City Tour Bus or a local taxi to the wharf.

places.name: 쁘띠프랑스
places.tip: A charming French cultural village inspired by 'The Little Prince', also a filming location for 'My Love from the Star'. Entry fee is 12,000 KRW. Best visited during the day to enjoy the colorful architecture and performances. Accessible via the Gapyeong City Tour Bus.

places.name: 아침고요수목원
places.tip: One of Korea's most beautiful private gardens, featuring various themed sections. Entry fee is 11,000 KRW. Visit in spring for flowers, autumn for fall foliage, or winter for the dazzling Lighting Festival. The Gapyeong City Tour Bus stops here.

places.name: 가평 레일바이크
places.tip: Enjoy a scenic 8km ride along an old railway track, offering beautiful views of the Bukhangang River. Prices are around 35,000 KRW for a 2-seater and 45,000 KRW for a 4-seater. Booking online in advance is recommended, especially on weekends and holidays.

places.name: 가평 탑랜드
places.tip: Experience thrilling activities like the Gapyeong Zip Line (about 40,000 KRW) soaring over the Bukhangang River, or enjoy various water leisure sports such as jet skis and banana boats during warmer months. It's a great spot for adventure seekers.

places.name: 자라섬
places.tip: Known for hosting the annual Jara Island International Jazz Festival and offering extensive camping facilities. Entry is free unless there's a special event. It's a peaceful spot for a walk or picnic, especially beautiful in spring and autumn. Easily accessible from Gapyeong Station.

places.name: 가평닭갈비막국수
places.tip: Savor authentic Chuncheon-style Dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and Makguksu (buckwheat noodles), signature dishes of the region. Expect to pay around 15,000-20,000 KRW per person. Many restaurants are located near Gapyeong Station or along the main roads.

places.name: 가평잣고을시장
places.tip: Explore a traditional local market where you can find fresh produce, street food, and Gapyeong's famous pine nuts. It's a great place to experience local life and pick up unique souvenirs. Visit on market days (usually 5-day intervals) for the fullest experience.

places.name: 더스테이 힐링파크
places.tip: A comprehensive resort offering a golf course, beautiful gardens, a cafe, and various relaxation facilities. It's ideal for a luxurious and peaceful retreat. Consider staying overnight or enjoying a meal at one of their upscale restaurants. A bit further out, so a taxi or private car is recommended.

places.name: 북한강카페
places.tip: Enjoy coffee and desserts with a picturesque view of the Bukhangang River. There are many such scenic cafes along the riverbanks in Gapyeong. Prices are typical for Korean cafes (5,000-8,000 KRW for a drink). Perfect for a relaxing break after sightseeing.

marketingCopy: Escape the bustling city to Gapyeong, a scenic haven in Gyeonggi-do, offering serene nature, iconic K-drama filming locations, and thrilling outdoor activities perfect for a refreshing getaway.

places.name: 동대문디자인플라자 (DDP)
places.tip: Explore this iconic futuristic landmark, a hub for design, art exhibitions, and cultural events. Check their website for current exhibitions, many of which are free or have a nominal fee.

places.name: 두타몰
places.tip: One of Dongdaemun's premier fashion malls, offering a wide range of trendy clothing, accessories, and cosmetics. It's open late, making it perfect for night owls.

places.name: 흥인지문
places.tip: Visit one of Seoul's original city gates, beautifully preserved and illuminated at night. It's a great spot for historical photos and understanding Seoul's past.

places.name: 동대문 패션타운 (평화시장)
places.tip: Experience a traditional wholesale market specializing in clothing, often open late into the night. It offers a glimpse into Seoul's bustling fashion industry and unique finds.

places.name: 동대문 완구거리
places.tip: A vibrant street filled with wholesale toy and stationery stores, perfect for finding unique souvenirs, gifts, or just enjoying a nostalgic stroll. Great for families and collectors.

places.name: 광장시장
places.tip: A must-visit for foodies, famous for its authentic Korean street food like Bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and Mayak Gimbap. Come hungry and explore the endless culinary delights.

places.name: 서울 성곽길 (흥인지문 구간)
places.tip: Walk a preserved section of the ancient Seoul City Wall near Dongdaemun for historical insight and scenic views of the city. Best enjoyed during cooler mornings or evenings.

places.name: 카페 DDP
places.tip: Conveniently located inside the Dongdaemun Design Plaza, this cafe offers a pleasant spot to rest and grab a coffee or light snack while admiring the unique architecture.

places.name: 동대문 닭한마리 골목
places.tip: Indulge in 'Dak Han Mari,' a whole chicken soup cooked at your table, a local specialty perfect for sharing. Many restaurants in this alley offer this hearty and delicious dish.

places.name: 롯데피트인 동대문점
places.tip: A modern shopping mall offering a diverse range of fashion brands, cosmetics, and lifestyle products. It's a great alternative to traditional markets for a comfortable shopping experience.

marketingCopy: Discover Dongdaemun, where ancient history meets futuristic design and vibrant night markets. Explore iconic architecture, shop for the latest trends, and savor delicious Korean street food around the clock.

places.name: 이화벽화마을 벽화
places.tip: Explore the vibrant murals and installations spread throughout the village. Visit on weekday mornings to avoid crowds and get the best photos. Remember to be respectful of residents' privacy and noise levels.

places.name: 낙산공원 이화동
places.tip: Climb to Naksan Park for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul, especially stunning at sunset. It's a free activity and offers a great perspective of the city.

places.name: 개뿔
places.tip: This charming cafe is famous for its rooftop seating that provides magnificent views over Seoul. It's an ideal spot to relax with a coffee or tea after exploring the village.

places.name: 이화중심
places.tip: Step into this cozy cafe for a taste of traditional Korean teas and desserts. It offers a quiet, artistic ambiance perfect for a peaceful break.

places.name: 이화동 맛집
places.tip: Discover authentic Korean home-style cooking at one of the small, family-run restaurants. Look for daily specials and enjoy a hearty meal at local prices.

places.name: 길거리 음식 노점
places.tip: Indulge in popular Korean street snacks like Tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) or Hotteok (sweet pancakes) from various vendors dotted throughout the village. Cash is often preferred.

places.name: 이화동 기념품 가게
places.tip: Browse for unique, handcrafted souvenirs and art pieces that reflect the village's artistic spirit. These make perfect gifts or mementos of your visit.

places.name: 이화동 갤러리
places.tip: Visit local galleries to appreciate contemporary art, often by local artists, with themes inspired by the village and its history. Entry is usually free.

places.name: 문구점
places.tip: Find quirky stationery, small art supplies, or unique crafts that embody the artistic vibe of Ihwa Mural Village. Great for creative gifts.

places.name: 이화벽화마을 포토존
places.tip: Seek out iconic photo spots like the 'Flower Stairs' or 'Fish Stairs' for memorable pictures. Be patient as these can get crowded and be mindful not to block residential entrances.

marketingCopy: Discover Ihwa Mural Village, a vibrant hillside neighborhood transformed into an open-air art gallery with colorful murals and sculptures. Perfect for photography enthusiasts and those seeking unique cultural experiences and stunning Seoul city views.

places.name: 어린왕자와 사막여우
places.nameEn: The Little Prince and Fox Photo Zone
places.tip: This iconic spot often has a queue; visit early in the morning or late afternoon for fewer crowds and better lighting for photos.

places.name: 감천문화마을 안내센터
places.tip: Start your visit here to grab a village map with a stamp tour (2,000 KRW), which guides you through key attractions and offers a fun way to explore.

places.name: 하늘마루
places.tip: Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the colorful village cascading down to the sea; it's a prime spot for photography, especially during sunset.

places.name: 감내맛집
places.tip: Savor authentic local Korean dishes like Bibimbap or Pajeon in this cozy restaurant, a great place to refuel after exploring the village.

places.name: 흙집카페
places.tip: Experience a traditional Korean 'loess house' while enjoying a coffee or tea, offering a unique blend of cultural immersion and relaxation.

places.name: 감천 박물관
places.tip: Delve into the fascinating history of Gamcheon Culture Village, from its origins as a refugee settlement to its vibrant artistic transformation. Entry is free.

places.name: 물고기자리 카페
places.tip: This charming cafe is known for its artistic interior and often features local artworks, providing a relaxing break with good views.

places.name: 감천문화마을 공중목욕탕
places.nameEn: Gamcheon Culture Village Public Bath Art Space
places.tip: Explore this creatively repurposed former public bathhouse, now an art exhibition space showcasing unique installations and reflecting the village's artistic spirit.

places.name: 감천문화마을 기념품점
places.tip: Find a wide array of handmade crafts, postcards, and quirky souvenirs created by local artists, perfect for taking a piece of Gamcheon home.

places.name: 아트샵
places.tip: Browse a diverse collection of paintings, sculptures, and unique art pieces, directly supporting the local artists who contribute to the village's charm.

marketingCopy: Step into a vibrant fairytale at Gamcheon Culture Village, a colorful hillside community transformed into an open-air museum. Explore whimsical street art, charming cafes, and breathtaking panoramic views that make it a photographer's paradise.

places.name: 관가정
places.tip: As a prime example of a noble Joseon-era house, explore its exterior and courtyard. The village itself has an entrance fee of approximately ₩4,000 for adults.

places.name: 무첨당
places.tip: This historically significant house showcases traditional Korean architecture. Respect residents' privacy as many houses are still lived in; avoid entering private sections.

places.name: 향단
places.tip: Admire the grandeur and unique layout of this iconic house from the outside. Best visited in spring or autumn for comfortable weather and beautiful scenery.

places.name: 양동마을 산책로
places.tip: Allow 2-3 hours to fully explore the village's winding paths and various sections. Wear comfortable shoes, as there are gentle inclines and unpaved sections.

places.name: 양동마을 민속박물관
places.tip: Start your visit here to gain insight into the village's history and culture. It provides excellent context before exploring the traditional houses.

places.name: 양동마을 전통찻집
places.tip: Enjoy a peaceful break with traditional Korean tea and snacks in a charming hanok setting. Expect prices for beverages to be around ₩5,000-₩8,000.

places.name: 양동마을 기념품점
places.tip: Discover unique handcrafted souvenirs, traditional pottery, and local goods near the village entrance. It's a great opportunity to find authentic Korean gifts.

places.name: 양동마을 식당
places.tip: Savor local Gyeongju dishes like Ssambap (rice wraps) or traditional stews at one of the eateries near the village entrance. Lunch prices typically range from ₩10,000-₩15,000 per person.

places.name: 양동마을 한지공예
places.tip: Inquire about traditional craft workshops, such as Hanji (Korean paper) making, which are occasionally offered. Participation fees usually range from ₩10,000-₩20,000.

places.name: 심수정
places.tip: Climb to this elegant pavilion for breathtaking panoramic views of the entire village and surrounding landscape – perfect for photography, especially during sunset.

marketingCopy: Step back in time at Yangdong Folk Village, a living UNESCO World Heritage site where the traditions and architecture of the Joseon Dynasty are beautifully preserved amidst stunning natural scenery.
